name: Question 15
problem:
$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)=2x(t)+y(t)+x(t)^{3} \\ {y}^{′}(t)=-2x(t)+y(t)^{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the system of differential equations above. What is the behavior of the system's solutions near the equilibrium ${x}^{∗}=[0,\text{ }0]^{T}?$$\,$
The equilibrium is an 
{{field-1}}{{field-2}}.
worked_solution:
The system can be rewritten in matrix form as 

$$
{x}^{′}=f(x)
$$

where $x=[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}]$ and 
$f(x)=[\begin{aligned}2x+y+{x}^{3} \\ -2x+{y}^{3}\end{aligned}].$

We need to compute the Jacobian matrix (or the total derivative) of $f(x).$ 

In our case, we have the following:

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y}\end{aligned}]
$$

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & =2+3{x}^{2},\, & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} & =1 \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & =-2,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y} & =3{y}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}2+3{x}^{2} & 1 \\ -2 & 3{y}^{2}\end{aligned}].
$$

Next, we evaluate the Jacobian at the equilibrium ${x}^{∗}=[0,\text{ }0]^{T}$ to get

$$
{f}^{′}({x}^{∗})=[\begin{aligned}2+0 & 1 \\ -2 & 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ -2 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the eigenvalues of the Jacobian matrix, we write down the characteristic equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}2-\lambda  & 1 \\ -2 & -\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (2-\lambda )(-\lambda )+2 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-2\lambda +2 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the equation, we get the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1,2}=1\pm i.$

Since we have two complex eigenvalues with positive real parts, our equilibrium is an $\text{unstable}$ $\text{spiral source}.$
